title: Ships Can't Sail Down Rapids... So We Built Water Elevators
sources: USACE Detroit District 'Frequently Asked Soo Locks Questions' / Soo Locks (Wikipedia) / saultstemarie.com FAQ: the St. Marys River drops about 21 feet from Lake Superior to Lake Huron at Sault Ste. Marie, Michigan; the locks lift and lower ships about 21 feet

USACE Detroit District Soo Locks FAQ / saultstemarie.com FAQ / Michigan State University 'The Soo Locks': no pumps are used; water flows by gravity through tunnels (culverts) in the lock walls when valves open

USACE Detroit District Soo Locks FAQ / saultstemarie.com / EUP News: about 22 million gallons of water fill the Poe Lock; the Poe Lock (1,200 ft long) is the one that takes the 1,000-foot lake freighters

Britannica 'Canal: Locks' / Wikipedia 'Lock (water navigation)' / USACE EM 1110-2-2703 'Lock Gates and Operating Equipment': miter gates meet in a V pointing upstream so the higher water presses them shut; they can only be opened once the water levels on both sides are equal
USACE Tulsa District 'How Locks Operate' / USGS 'Navigation' water-science page: a lock is a chamber with gates at both ends; filling or emptying it raises or lowers the boat to the next water level

lines.text: If you sail a ship out of Lake Superior, the river in front of you drops twenty-one feet.
lines.caps: If you sail a ship | out of Lake Superior, | the river in front of you | drops 21 feet.

lines.text: And a thousand-foot freighter can't just ride down the rapids.
lines.caps: And a 1,000-foot freighter | can't just ride | down the rapids.

lines.text: So, in Michigan, engineers built the Soo Locks, a giant concrete box with gates at both ends.
lines.caps: So, in Michigan, | engineers built the Soo Locks, | a giant concrete box | with gates at both ends.

lines.text: The ship sails in, and the gates behind it swing shut.
lines.caps: The ship sails in, | and the gates behind it | swing shut.

lines.text: But here's the crazy part. There are no pumps.
lines.caps: But here's the crazy part. | There are no pumps.

lines.text: Valves open in the walls, and gravity drains the water down to the lower lake.
lines.caps: Valves open in the walls, | and gravity drains the water | down to the lower lake.

lines.text: And the ship slowly sinks with it, like an elevator made of water.
lines.caps: And the ship slowly sinks with it, | like an elevator | made of water.

lines.text: But now the gates are holding back a wall of water two stories high.
lines.caps: But now the gates | are holding back | a wall of water | two stories high.

lines.text: So, the gates meet in a V that points upstream, and the water pushes them shut.
lines.caps: So, the gates meet in a V | that points upstream, | and the water | pushes them shut.

lines.text: That's why they only open when the water on both sides is level.
lines.caps: That's why they only open | when the water | on both sides is level.

lines.text: Filling the biggest lock here takes about twenty-two million gallons, all by gravity.
lines.caps: Filling the biggest lock here | takes about | 22 million gallons, | all by gravity.

lines.text: You see, the lock never lifts the ship. Water just finds its level.
lines.caps: You see, the lock | never lifts the ship. | Water just | finds its level.

lines.text: That's why ships can climb a river without a single pump.
lines.caps: That's why ships | can climb a river | without a single pump.
